summary: Cold Q4 bidirectional walk fails Quality Interlock. Core API claim fencing, HMAC delivery, quota, pause/resume, DLQ transition, replay auth, and audit families are largely discoverable from instruction.md plus delivery-contract.md and meaningfully tested, but material gaps remain: UI claim/error obligations are only substring-grepped (vacuous), deliver lease_mismatch is untested, replay lease/attempt_count semantics and backoff steps after the first interval are untested, CLI coverage stops at health/enqueue/claim despite a full public CLI contract, and seed P2P asserts undocumented catalog cardinality floors. Instruction shape and delegated-contract boundary are otherwise sound.

evidence.observation: Two short paragraphs plus four bullets: repair API/CLI/UI against /app/outbox/docs/delivery-contract.md; graded path is claim→deliver with OUTBOX_SYNC=1; env vars OUTBOX_DB/ADDR/DATA/TOKEN/SYNC; schema boot, seed tooling and image-seeded DB under /app/outbox/data; UI from /app/outbox/ui; concurrent claims 409; paused rejects claims; rebuild outboxd/outboxctl; UI field names and error surfacing.

Binding routes/payloads/leases/HMAC/backoff/DLQ/replay/quota/pause/audit/env/CLI/UI. States lease_mismatch for complete and deliver; replay clears lease and leaves attempt_count unchanged; backoff [5,15,45,120,300]; seed DB plus bin/seed and scripts/seed.sh without numeric catalog floors; UI claim JSON must use lease_owner/lease_seconds; errors to #error-box.

F2P modules cover tenant/endpoint, enqueue/idempotency/disabled, list/get/stats, claim/renew/409/expired reclaim, pause/resume, complete lease_mismatch, signed deliver, first-backoff+DLQ, attempts, quota enqueue/deliver/complete, audit actions, replay 401/200, CLI health/enqueue/claim, UI JS substrings. P2P covers health, schema file, UI index title/error-box, 404 not_found, invalid payload 400, tenant list, enqueue audit endpoint_id, seed artifact presence with tenants>=6/endpoints>=18/events>=100.

UI tests only assert lease_owner/lease_seconds/error-box/textContent/data.error substrings in app.js; no live claim POST body or error-box DOM behavior. Replay success asserts status pending and replay audit only.

Public UI helper currently posts claim JSON keys owner/seconds (not lease_owner/lease_seconds) and does not write #error-box; confirms F2P UI intent, and that string-presence tests would accept non-behavioral fixes.
Seed P2P asserts sqlite counts tenants>=6, endpoints>=18, events>=100; CLI test only exercises health, enqueue, claim.
Classification-only map aligns named F2P/P2P cases to R_* families; used solely to label ownership, not as a requirement source.

Material phantom tests, untested material requirements, vacuous coverage of graded obligations, and grading-relevant ambiguity require REVISE; PASS needs exhaustive matrices with empty BLOCKING_FINDING_IDS.
Instruction owns material ask; delegated docs may hold protocol/schema; every tested behavior must be discoverable; implementation diagnosis and prompt-extension docs are defects.

findings.criterion: Material UI field-name and error-surfacing requirements need meaningful behavioral assertions, not vacuous source greps.
findings.why_it_matters: Contract and instruction require claim POST JSON to use lease_owner/lease_seconds and API errors shown via #error-box. The verifier only checks that those substrings (or showError/textContent/data.error) appear in app.js. A non-compliant helper that still posts owner/seconds (as the starter does) can pass by adding unused string literals, so the graded UI obligations are effectively untested.
findings.minimal_remediation: Q2: drive a live UI/helper path (or parse the claim request construction) asserting the JSON body keys and that a non-2xx API error populates #error-box textContent. Keep F2P against the broken owner/seconds starter.
findings.regression_risk: Low if behavioral asserts replace greps without prescribing helper function names.

findings.criterion: Every material fencing rule in the solver-visible contract must have a meaningful assertion.
findings.why_it_matters: Claim fencing states only the current lease_owner may complete or deliver; mismatch → 409 lease_mismatch. Verifier asserts that for complete only. A deliver path that ignores lease ownership can still pass the suite.
findings.minimal_remediation: Q2: add F2P that claims as owner A then POST /deliver as owner B and expects 409 lease_mismatch without marking delivered.
findings.regression_risk: Low; mirrors existing complete mismatch coverage.

findings.criterion: Material replay semantics stated in the binding contract must be tested when they change accepted state.
findings.why_it_matters: Replay must set pending, leave attempt_count unchanged, clear lease, and set next_attempt_at=now. The passing test only checks status pending plus a replay audit action. Implementations that reset attempt_count or leave a lease can still score 1.
findings.minimal_remediation: Q2: after authorized replay, assert attempt_count unchanged vs pre-replay, lease_owner/lease_until null, and next_attempt_at near now.
findings.regression_risk: Low if assertions stay semantic and tolerate RFC3339 formatting.

findings.criterion: Documented backoff schedule is a material operational requirement; partial coverage of only the first interval leaves later steps untested.
findings.why_it_matters: Contract requires next_attempt_at offsets [5,15,45,120,300] then stay at 300. The suite only bounds the first failure (~5s) before forcing DLQ at max_attempts=2. Wrong later schedule values never fail grading.
findings.minimal_remediation: Q2: with higher max_attempts, assert at least the second (15s) and/or plateau-at-300 behavior, or metamorphic check that attempt n maps to the published table.
findings.regression_risk: Medium if timing windows are too tight; use deterministic clock seams or wide bounds already used for the first interval.

findings.criterion: Instruction requires CLI brought back in line with the public CLI contract; graded CLI coverage must not stop at a thin smoke subset when the contract lists operator commands.
findings.why_it_matters: delivery-contract.md publishes outboxctl deliver/replay/pause/resume/audit/tenants list as public operator surface. Instruction says repair API, CLI, and UI. Only health + enqueue + claim are exercised. Broken CLI deliver/replay/pause can still pass.
findings.minimal_remediation: Q2: extend CLI F2P to at least one mutation beyond claim (e.g. deliver or pause/resume) and one authenticated replay, or narrow the solver-visible CLI contract/instruction to the actually graded subcommands.
findings.regression_risk: Low if added commands reuse existing API fixtures; do not invent private CLI flags.

findings.criterion: phantom-spec: verifier must not enforce undocumented numeric floors as pass/fail criteria.
findings.why_it_matters: Solver-visible material requires keeping the image-seeded default DB and seed tooling available, but never states tenants>=6, endpoints>=18, or events>=100. Those floors are private fixture checksums: an operator-preserving smaller reseeds/truncation fails grading without a discoverable cardinality rule.
findings.minimal_remediation: Q2: assert presence of seeded DB + seed binary/script and non-empty catalog tables, or Q3: publish the graded minimum catalog sizes in delivery-contract.md if those floors are truly required.
findings.regression_risk: Low if presence/non-empty checks replace hard floors; medium if floors are documented and become a new public obligation.

findings.criterion: Auth contract lists missing or invalid bearer → 401; only missing token is asserted.
findings.why_it_matters: Invalid token handling could diverge from missing-token behavior without failing tests. Advisory because missing-token 401 already covers the primary graded auth gate.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional Q2: one replay with Authorization Bearer wrong-token expecting 401 unauthorized.

findings.criterion: Compact nested sorted-key signing is stated exactly; only a flat object is signed in tests.
findings.why_it_matters: Nested-object key sorting could be wrong while flat payloads still pass. Advisory relative to the already-strong flat canonical/HMAC assert.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional Q2: enqueue a nested payload and assert compact body bytes plus matching signature.

findings.criterion: Default lease_seconds=30 when omitted or <1 is untested.
findings.why_it_matters: All claim tests supply positive lease_seconds. Defaulting bugs would not fail grading. Advisory.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional Q2: claim with omitted or 0 lease_seconds and assert ~30s lease_until.

findings.criterion: Newest-first ordering for tenant event lists and audit is stated but not asserted.
findings.why_it_matters: Ordering mistakes would still pass membership-only checks. Advisory for operator UX ordering.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional Q2: enqueue/audit two items and assert newest-first order.

findings.criterion: Paused endpoints may still accept enqueue; positive case not tested.
findings.why_it_matters: A pause implementation that also blocks enqueue would violate the contract but is not caught. Advisory asymmetry vs disabled-enqueue coverage.
findings.minimal_remediation: Optional Q2: pause then enqueue expecting 201 pending while claim still 409.

findings.criterion: complete outcome=failed resulting status/audit is under-specified relative to deliver.fail/dlq paths and is untested.
findings.why_it_matters: complete accepts outcome failed, but the contract does not clearly say whether status becomes failed vs pending-with-backoff vs dlq, and no test drives that branch. Advisory unless that path becomes graded.
findings.minimal_remediation: Q3: clarify complete-as-failed state machine, or Q2: avoid grading that branch and keep deliver-path failures as the authoritative failure surface.
findings.regression_risk: Low if left ungraded; medium if a new status rule is introduced.
